title: Account Locked
intro: An email just landed. Your bank, it says, has locked your account.
Tap anything that looks odd to sniff it closer. Pin what is suspicious, clear what is harmless.
When you are sure, decide what to do.

notify.text: Your account has been LOCKED. Act now.

subject.text: Your account has been LOCKED - act now

p: or your account will be permanently closed.

p.text: online banking login and card PIN
Do not contact your branch. This process is automatic.

addr.label: Not the bank's domain
addr.lens: The email comes from orrin-bank-help.com. The bank's real address ends in orrin.app.
addr.why: Look-alike sender addresses add extra words. Check the part after the @, letter by letter.

deadline.label: Deadline and threat
deadline.lens: Two hours, or the account is closed for good.
deadline.why: A hard deadline is built to stop you thinking. Real banks do not work this way.

link.label: Look-alike link
link.lens: The button really goes to orrin-bank-help.com/restore.
link.why: Never log in through a link in an email. Type the bank's address or use its app.

login.label: Asks for login and PIN
login.lens: The page wants your login and your card PIN.
login.why: No real bank asks for your PIN. Anyone who does is a scammer.

nocall.label: "Do not contact your branch"
nocall.lens: The email tells you not to check with your branch.
nocall.why: Scammers block your way to a check. A real bank is happy for you to check.

greet.label: "Dear Customer"
greet.why: Many real emails use your name, but a generic hello alone is not proof of a scam.

subject.label: Capital letters
subject.why: Shouting alone proves nothing. The threats and the link do.

from.label: Bank name
from.lens: The sender name says Orrin Bank Security.
from.why: A display name is easy to type. Look at the address behind it.

actions.label: Open the Orrin app myself and look
Report it as phishing and delete it

trap.title: Orrin Bank · Restore access
trap.ask: Enter your online banking login and card PIN to restore access.

block_report.line: Reported as phishing. The bank's security team had the fake address blocked by lunchtime.

verify.line: The app showed no lock and no warning. The email was fake. Case cracked.

ignore.line: You stayed safe. The fake address is still sending the same email to thousands of others.

go_ahead.line: The page copied your login and PIN. The real account was emptied in minutes.

what_if.go_ahead: Opening the bank's own app would have shown no lock, and no problem at all.
what_if.ignore: Forwarding the email to the bank's fraud address helps get the fake site taken down.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting the email as well protects other people.

golden_rule: Never log in through a link in an email. Open the bank's own app or type its address yourself.

quick_check.q: An email says your account is locked and you have two hours to log in through a button. What do you do?

options.text: Click fast, two hours is short
Reply asking if it is real
Open the bank's own app yourself, and report the email
Forward it to a friend to check

quick_check.explain: The deadline and the link are the trap. Your bank's own app shows the truth in seconds.

hints.nudge: Look at the address the email really came from.

kit.title: What the bank and consumer advice say

How to check an alarming message
